thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gen-runtime p99 latency breach detected in prod-eu-west (2026-04-22T09:14:04Z). Symptoms: p99 > 3.5s, rising 5xx, prefetch queue growth. Paging on-call.

rachel (oncall): on it. main dashboards look noisy. any recent deploys? customer reports?

tom (runtime): no deploys in last hour. quick probe shows continuous-batcher queueing ballooned and average microbatch size jumped. KV cache insert rate and eviction rate spiked concurrently. snippets: 
```
2026-04-22T09:13:58Z host=gen-runtime-12 inflight=3900 microbatch.avg=812 kv.cache.size=1_320_980 evict_rps=5_900
2026-04-22T09:14:04Z batch.p99=3.86s queue_depth=13_800
2026-04-22T09:14:20Z http 502 x 52
```

rachel (oncall): yikes. could be the classic high-cardinality prefixes -> cache blowout -> batching amplification. evelyn, any infra thoughts?

evelyn (infra): agree w/ tom. quick mitigations: 1) cap max microbatch to reduce per-batch work; 2) flip continuous-batching off for the affected pool; 3) enable a soft-insert quota for KV to slow new prefixes. 1 is fastest to ship.

rachel (oncall): do 1 now. leave 2/3 as follow-ups. please run the config change and call out the change id.

evelyn (infra): applying patch: 
```
# cap microbatch for gen-runtime pool in eu-west
redwoodctl config set runtime.continuous_batch.max_microbatch 120 --env prod --scope gen-runtime-pool-eu-west
```

deploy-bot: config apply started (chg chg-20260422-05). rolling config to 48 nodes in eu-west. expected converge ~40s.

rachel (oncall): watching p99 / queue depth / evict_rps.

tom (runtime): metrics: p99 fell 3.86s -> 640ms within 70s; queue depth dropped to ~1.2k; evict_rps down to ~480. dropping 5xxs.

mark (cs): customer impact: two tenants (cust-omega, cust-sierra) reported timeouts around 09:14-09:18 UTC. CS has opened tickets and sent initial status notes. no data exposure.

rachel (oncall): created incident INC-2026-0422-11 and attached traces + top request ids. assigning to @tom and @evelyn for root cause and follow-ups. brief summary: "microbatch inflation under high concurrency + KV insert storm -> eviction surge -> p99 performance cliff".

evelyn (infra): short-term follow-up list: 
- add feature flag for per-model KV soft quota (FF rollout)
- make KV GC insert throttling backpressure-aware
- tune batch selection heuristics to bias for latency when evict_rps or cpu_pressure high
- add canary tests that simulate high-cardinality prefix traffic

tom (runtime): i'll prototype a router-side jitter smoothing buffer (small delay with randomness) and change runtime heuristics to cap microbatch growth aggressively when eviction or GC stalls are detected. will open PRs.

rachel (oncall): handing off to @sam (starts shift in ~15m). handoff notes:
- incident mitigated: p99 ~640ms after change chg-20260422-05
- mitigation: runtime.continuous_batch.max_microbatch=120 (chg-20260422-05)
- affected customers: cust-omega, cust-sierra (CS notified)
- action items: FF for KV quota, GC backpressure, router jitter smoothing, postmortem in 72h

sam (oncall-next): ack. i'll monitor dashboards for the next window and follow up on INC-2026-0422-11. please paste flamegraphs and the top 10 request ids into the ticket.

rachel (oncall): uploaded traces, flamegraphs, and request ids to the incident ticket and pinned the mitigation commands to the ticket. marking paging mitigated but leaving incident open for RCA.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. postmortem requested within 72h. tags: perf, kv-cache, continuous-batching, high-concurrency.

dave (sre): recommend load-tests that generate thousands of distinct prefix keys per second at varying arrival skews to validate heuristics. i'll add an SRE job for that and gate the FF rollout behind it.

tom (runtime): noted. i'll start PRs for: per-conn prefix cap, runtime GC signals, and router smoothing. linking all to INC-2026-0422-11.

evelyn (infra): i'll prepare the FF for soft KV quotas and a safe rollback plan.

mark (cs): i'll draft a customer-facing post-incident note to send once the postmortem is published.

rachel (oncall): thanks all. leaving the channel but will be around for postmortem prep. :white_check_mark:
